queries.query: the Pythagorean rule of reviewing each day before sleep, asking what wrong was committed, what was accomplished, and what duty was left undone
queries.note: The nightly examination; 'Wherein have I done amiss? What have I done? What have I omitted that I ought to have done?' reworded, 'reprimand thyself severely' dropped.

queries.query: Hierocles dividing the Golden Verses into a part that shapes decent human beings through practical virtue and a part that lifts them toward godhood through contemplation
queries.note: 'The making of Good Men' / 'make Good Men into Gods' paraphrased; Hierocles and the work's title kept as reader-honest anchors.

queries.query: the Pythagorean symbol forbidding one to cut fire with a sword, read as a warning not to provoke a wrathful man with stinging words
queries.note: Symbol 9; the maxim itself kept as a title any reader knows, the explanation's 'opposing sharp words to a man full of fire and wrath' reworded.

queries.query: why the sentences of Sextus hold it perilous to discuss divinity before the multitude, even to say what is true
queries.note: 'Speak not of God to every man', 'the danger is not small' paraphrased; Sextus kept as the collection's name.

queries.query: what daily disciplines train the soul toward virtue
queries.note: The Stobaeus ethical sentences answer this, but so does nearly every tradition. No target — graded post-hoc.

queries.query: can a human being become like God through wisdom and right living
queries.note: Sextus: the wise man resembles God; deification through virtue is pan-traditional. No target — graded post-hoc.
